:::{#def-integral-nonneg}
#### Integral of a non-negative function

Let $(S, \mathscr{S}, \mu)$ be a [measure space](#def-measure-space),
and let $f : S \to [0, \infty)$ be [measurable](#def-measurable-function).
The **integral** of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ is

$$
\int_S f \, d\mu \eqdef
\sup \set{\sum_{i=1}^{n} \paren{\inf_{s \in A_i} f(s)} \mu(A_i)}
$$

where the [supremum](algebra.qmd#def-supremum) is over all ways
of writing $S$ as the union of finitely many nonempty
[pairwise disjoint](#def-pairwise-disjoint) sets $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ in $\mathscr{S}$,
and each $\inf_{s \in A_i} f(s)$ is the [infimum](algebra.qmd#def-infimum)
of the values of $f$ on $A_i$.
In the sums, $0 \cdot \infty \eqdef 0$, and $x \cdot \infty \eqdef \infty$ for $x > 0$;
the supremum is $\infty$ if some sum is $\infty$.
The integral is also written $\int_S f(s) \, d\mu(s)$.

[@billingsley1995probability, Section 15]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-integral-nonneg-lower-sums}
#### Each sum is a lower estimate

Each sum in @def-integral-nonneg splits $S$ into pieces
and weights each piece $A_i$ by the smallest value $f$ approaches on it,
so each sum is at most the integral.
For Lebesgue measure on a closed interval $[a, b]$
and a function $f \ge 0$ that has a
[Riemann integral](calculus.qmd#def-riemann-integral) on $[a, b]$,
the two integrals agree:
$\int_{[a, b]} f \, d\lambda = \int_a^b f(x) \, dx$
(see [Wikipedia: Lebesgue integral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebesgue_integral)).

:::
